items.name: Cabot L102 - Discovery Bar
items.description:
The Discovery Bar is a flexible serpentine table, which can be used for a variety of technology demonstrations and/or displays. It includes two projectors and large screens - allowing input
from several sources (the resident computer or personal devices). The Discovery Bar is a great place to present and promote library, technology, and research projects.

• There is one floor outlet in this space. 
  • Students are welcome to use the Discovery Bar as a standing desk when there is not an event or activity.
  • The Discovery Bar is not a quiet presentation space. Presenters should be prepared for a certain amount of noise from patrons entering and exiting the library as well as from the adjacent Clover café.
  • ♿This room is wheelchair accessible. Find out more information on accessible building entrances and paths.

items.name: Cabot L103 - The Ice Cube
items.description: The Ice Cube, aka the Consultation Room, is a great location to meet for individual and small group assistance from a librarian, technical specialist, or a representative from our program partners. It seats up to four people at a round table. It may be utilized together with the Discovery Bar to display a related slide, video, etc. drawing the public’s attention to a more hands-on drop-in session in the Ice Cube.

items.name: Cabot LL01 — Media Studio A
items.description: Cabot Media Studio A comfortably seats two people and offers the option of either an overhead camera or a view from the back of the room camera. It includes green and grey screen backgrounds.
items.what_you_need_to_know:
Find out more about the studio equipment and booking process. 

  • Media Studios are available for all members of the Harvard community to use.
  • You should come with your own NTFS- or FAT-formatted hard drive for storing your video files. If needed, flash drives can be borrowed from the Access Services desk on the lower level.
  • Reservation priority is given for academic use. 
  • Rooms may be reserved for a maximum of three hours at a time, no more than 14 days in advance.
  • Reservations for consecutive, concurrent, or recurring meetings are not permitted.
  • Cabot's media studios are largely self service. Student consultants are available to help during the academic year.

Training

Before booking a media studio you must complete a 30-minute training session. Trainings are offered by appointment, Monday through Thursday, 9am- 5pm. Contact cablib@fas.harvard.edu to set up a training time.

Booking

After completing training, you may book either studio for two hours at a time. To make a reservation, email cablib@fas.harvard.edu at least one week in advance with the following information:

  1. Which studio you would like to book
  2. A short description of your project
  3. Preferred dates and times for use
  4. Setup requests and special technological needs

The reserver takes full responsibility for loss or damage to equipment, cables, cameras, furniture and all other items in the studio. Fines will be assessed by Harvard Library for any damage detected, and can be levied up to one month after the reservation is completed.

items.name: Fine Arts Library Study Carrels
items.description: A study carrel fits one person comfortably around a private desk with shelf space to hold research materials. The Fine Arts Library houses 24 study carrels on the ground floor of stacks. These reservable, individual study spaces are in high demand throughout the school year, and applications are reviewed and carrels assigned on a first-come, first-serve basis. Note: Many libraries within the Harvard Library system offer reservable study carrels. Find the right fit by exploring each library's study carrel locations and policies.
items.what_you_need_to_know:
• Applications for carrels are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis. Carrel assignments are typically from September-August of the following year. Assignments must be renewed annually by April 30th.
  • To request a carrel, please fill out the Fine Arts Library Carrel and Shelf Request Form.
  • See also: Accessibility at Harvard Library

Fine Arts Library Carrel Policy

All carrel holders agree to abide by the following rules and regulations. Violation of these rules may result in loss of carrel privileges.

  • Carrel Assignments: The Fine Arts Library has a limited number of study carrels. Priority is given to graduate students and faculty members from the History of Art and Architecture Department (including dual degree students) and curators from the Harvard Art Museums. Other Harvard affiliates and independent researchers with a need to conduct long-term research with FAL collections may also be given consideration.
  • Active Use: Carrels are intended for active use. Infrequent users may request a hold shelf to store FAL materials for their research. If you are not actively using your carrel or are not in residence for a semester or more, please contact FAL Access Services so that the carrel can be reassigned, since there is usually a waiting list. Library staff can generate a list of all books charged to your carrel, so that you can reassemble your carrel at a later date. You may re-apply for a carrel upon your return.
  • Charging Items: All materials at a carrel must be properly charged to that carrel, rather than to your personal library account. Books charged to a carrel are not allowed to leave the building. If you want to take a book out of the library, you must check it out to your personal library account. You are fully responsible for the loss of any personal books or materials charged to your personal library account, including books from any other library and books received via interlibrary loan or Borrow Direct. Due to security risks involved, we strongly recommend that you keep at your carrel only those materials charged to that carrel. Due to space limitations, no more than 50 books may be charged to a carrel at one time.
  • Personal Items: The Fine Arts Library cannot guarantee the security of personal belongings, including personal books, left in carrels. Do not leave your personal items unattended.
  • Recalls: All materials charged to a carrel are subject to recall and removal by library staff. If you are a carrel holder and you recall an item already charged to another carrel or hold shelf, you will be asked to use the item at the carrel/shelf to which it is currently charged.
  • Inspections: Fine Arts Library staff reserve the right to inspect carrels routinely and remove any uncharged FAL books.
  • Courtesy to Other Patrons: Carrels are intended for quiet reading and research only and should not be used for conferences or long conversations. Other patrons may sit at carrels when they are not being used by the carrel holder. However, carrel holders have seating priority at their own carrels.
  • Carrel Maintenance: Carrel holders have a responsibility to keep their assigned space neat and tidy. Books should be shelved properly, upright with the spines visible. Improper shelving may cause damage to books, thereby incurring costs for rebinding or replacement. Do not store any materials on the floor. Use the trash receptacles provided to dispose of unwanted items.
  • Beverage Policy: Only water in a tight container with a secure lid is allowed in the stacks and carrels. Learn more about our beverage policy on our About page.
  • Prohibitions: Eating, smoking, and talking on cell phones is prohibited in the stacks.

items.what_you_need_to_know:

items.name: Tozzer Study Carrels
items.description: At Tozzer, there are 26 study carrels available for assignment, located along the perimeter of the ground floor. Carrels are to be used for independent study and research. Books (both personally and library-owned) may be kept at your carrel, under the condition that all library books are checked out to you and that your possessions do not overflow your area.
items.what_you_need_to_know:
Application Process: For carrel assignments, please apply here. To maximize your chances to receive a carrel for the academic year, we recommend that you apply at the beginning of the fall semester. Once we have received your request, we will be in touch with further details. 

Assignment Priority will be given to:

  1. Graduate students and senior thesis writers in Harvard's Anthropology and Human Evolutionary Biology departments
  2. Graduate students and senior thesis writers from other departments, but whose primary research topics are covered by Tozzer's collections
  3. Researchers affiliated with the Peabody Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology and the Harvard University Native American Program
  4. Other researchers conducting long-term research that need to use Tozzer collections

Please Note

  • There may be times that we ask you to share your carrel with one other researcher. We will notify you if a second person is assigned to your carrel.
  • Carrels are intended for active use as a workspace. If library staff notice that you are not regularly using your assigned carrel for this purpose, we will ask you to vacate your carrel and transfer your materials to a hold shelf. If you know that you will not be actively using your carrel or plan to be away for a semester or more, please contact Tozzer Access Services to discuss your options.
  • See also: Accessibility at Harvard Library.

Assignment Periods

Academic Year: September 1st through May 31st

  • If you are assigned a carrel for the academic year, you must vacate or renew the carrel by May 31st (unless you are assigned a carrel for the summer term). Carrels not renewed will be cleaned out by library staff.
  • If you wish to be assigned a carrel during the next academic year (but not during the summer), you may renew your assignment under the condition that you vacate the carrel from June 1st until August 31st.

Summer Term: June 1st through August 31st

  • If you are assigned a carrel for the summer term, you must vacate the carrel by August 31st (unless you have renewed the carrel for the next academic year). Carrels that have not been renewed will be cleaned out by library staff.

Carrel Renewals

For any questions and concerns, please email us (TozzerLibrary@fas.harvard.edu) or speak with any staff member at the Tozzer Circulation Desk. To renew your carrel, please contact us before the end of your current assignment.

• ♿ This room is accessible for people using wheelchairs or other mobility devices. Find more details about accessible building information on the Harvard accessibility map.

Location

Phillips Reading Room Policy

  • All materials must be used in the Phillips Reading Room and returned to a staff member at the Phillips Reading Room Desk.
  • Please observe any special handling indicated by the reading room staff.
  • The last paging request is taken one hour prior to closing and all materials must be returned to the desk 15 minutes prior to closing.
  • Readers interested in photoduplication should consult with the reading room staff. Imaging Services are also available, inquire at the Phillips Reading Room desk.
  • If you do not have a Harvard ID, you must present a current Widener Library Reading Room Card in order to request items from the stacks or depository.
  • All requests must be submitted in person, including those for Harvard Depository items.

items.name: Widener and Pusey Study Carrels
items.description:
A study carrel fits one person comfortably around a private desk with shelf space to hold research materials. These reservable, individual study spaces are in high demand throughout the school year, so more than one person may be assigned to each carrel.

Study carrels in the Widener stacks are available for 1) Harvard College seniors, 2) graduate students, 3) faculty, and 4) post-doctoral fellows who are conducting research and need to hold Widener books for an extended period of time.
items.what_you_need_to_know:
• To request a study carrel, fill out the Widener Library Carrel Application Form.  
  • Many libraries within the Harvard Library system offer reservable study carrels. Find the right fit by exploring each library's study carrel locations and policies.
  • Carrels are only available when the library is open. See library hours. 
  • See information about accessibility of Library buildings on the Accessibility at Harvard Library page.

Pusey Study Carrel Location

The Pusey study carrels are located on levels P2 and P3 in the Pusey Library stacks, which are accessible through the Widener Library stacks. Pusey study carrels are not accessible through the main Pusey Library entrance. 

Widener/Pusey Carrel Policy

All carrel holders agree to abide by the following rules and regulations. Violation of these rules may result in loss of carrel privileges. Widener Library is not responsible for lost or missing items left at/in carrels.

  • Charging Items: Only library materials properly charged to a carrel at the Widener Library circulation desk may be kept at that carrel. Due to security risks, uncharged library materials including ones charged to your personal ID will be removed. Personal books may be left at a carrel.
  • Recalls: Items on loan to your carrel are subject to recall and recall-late-return fine. You'll receive a recall notice and you are responsible for returning recalled items as you would for items checked out to your HUID. You may also forward recall notices to library_billing@harvard.edu for us to pull the books for you in which case the forward date will be considered the return date.
  • Shared Carrel: Due to high demand, more than one user will be assigned to each carrel. Please do not remove or interfere with materials left by others. Due to space limitations, carrel holders may utilize no more than 50% of his/her carrel shelving space at any given time. Do not leave personal items unattended.
  • Cabinet: Access code to a cabinet is available in the carrel holder’s Inscriptio account. This is shared among individuals assigned to each carrel, so do not leave valuables in a locked cabinet. Storing library materials in the locked cabinet is not allowed. Widener Library reserves the right to inspect locked cabinets and remove library material. 
  • Neatness: Carrels are inspected routinely and any unwanted or unsightly materials will be removed. Use bulletin boards at each carrel: do not post anything to library walls.
  • Talking: Noise levels must be held to a minimum. Conferences should not be held at carrel.
  • Eating, drinking, smoking, photography, cell phones: Usage of these is prohibited in the stacks. Food may be taken to the café on the ground floor and designated cell phone use areas are located in the outside vestibule of the main entrance, the café or the corridor to the Mass Ave Entrance on the ground floor, including the public telephone alcove.
